title: Normalized adjunction comparisons across equivalences preserve compositors and inverse mates
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ and $\overline{\mathcal A},\overline{\mathcal B},\overline{\mathcal C},\overline{\mathcal D}$ be categories, with specified equivalences $E_A,E_B,E_C,E_D$ between corresponding categories. Composition in this statement is functional: $VU=V\circ U$. Use the mate bijection and its inverse given by unit insertion and counit contraction [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate].

(1) For specified adjunctions $J:\mathcal A\rightleftarrows\mathcal B:U$ and $\bar J:\overline{\mathcal A}\rightleftarrows\overline{\mathcal B}:\bar U$, and a natural isomorphism $u:E_AU\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar U E_B$, there is a unique natural isomorphism $j:E_BJ\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar J E_A$ such that $j^{-1}$ has mate $u$. It identifies the full adjunction Hom bijections and both their units and counits. The analogous assertion holds for $J':\mathcal C\rightleftarrows\mathcal D:U'$, $\bar J':\overline{\mathcal C}\rightleftarrows\overline{\mathcal D}:\bar U'$ and $u':E_CU'\cong\bar U'E_D$, giving $j'$.

(2) These normalized comparisons preserve adjoint compositors. More precisely, let $\mathcal A_i,\overline{\mathcal A}_i$ ($0\leq i\leq2$) have equivalences $E_i$, specified adjunctions $L_{ij}:\mathcal A_i\rightleftarrows\mathcal A_j:R_{ji}$ and their barred counterparts for $i<j$, right comparisons $r_{ij}:E_iR_{ji}\cong\bar R_{ji}E_j$, and normalized left comparisons $c_{ij}:E_jL_{ij}\cong\bar L_{ij}E_i$ from (1). Let $\delta:R_{10}R_{21}\cong R_{20}$ and $\bar\delta:\bar R_{10}\bar R_{21}\cong\bar R_{20}$ be specified isomorphisms satisfying
$$ (\bar\delta E_2)\circ(\bar R_{10}r_{12})\circ(r_{01}R_{21})=r_{02}\circ E_0(\delta). $$
Let $a:L_{12}L_{01}\cong L_{02}$ and $\bar a:\bar L_{12}\bar L_{01}\cong\bar L_{02}$ be the adjoint compositors, whose conjugates are $\delta^{-1}$ and $\bar\delta^{-1}$ under the respective composite and direct adjunctions. Then
$$c_{02}\circ E_2(a)=(\bar a E_0)\circ(\bar L_{12}c_{01})\circ(c_{12}L_{01}).$$

(3) In the four-category setting of (1), let $P:\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$, $Q:\mathcal B\to\mathcal D$, $\bar P:\overline{\mathcal A}\to\overline{\mathcal C}$, $\bar Q:\overline{\mathcal B}\to\overline{\mathcal D}$ be functors with isomorphisms $p:E_CP\cong\bar P E_A$, $q:E_DQ\cong\bar Q E_B$. Let $b:PU\to U'Q$ and $\bar b:\bar P\bar U\to\bar U'\bar Q$ satisfy
$$(\bar b E_B)\circ(\bar P u)\circ(pU)=(\bar U' q)\circ(u'Q)\circ E_C(b).$$
Write $\beta:J'P\to QJ$ and $\bar\beta:\bar J'\bar P\to\bar Q\bar J$ for their inverse mates. Then the actual transformations satisfy
$$(\bar Q j)\circ(qJ)\circ E_D(\beta)=(\bar\beta E_A)\circ(\bar J'p)\circ(j'P).$$
Thus $\beta$ is invertible if and only if $\bar\beta$ is invertible. The statements use the canonical functor associators throughout, without requiring any equivalence, unit, counit or comparison to be an identity.

proof.text: Put $\alpha=\operatorname{mate}^{-1}(u):\bar J E_A\to E_BJ$ using [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Apply [lem-stage3-inverse-mate-equivalences] with $(L_1,R_1,L_2,R_2,G,H)=(J,U,\bar J,\bar U,E_A,E_B)$: its two vertical functors are equivalences and its right square is precisely the given isomorphism $u$. Thus $\alpha$ is invertible. Set $j=\alpha^{-1}$. Injectivity of the mate bijection gives uniqueness, including the specified normalization. Repeat with $(J',U',\bar J',\bar U',E_C,E_D,u')$ to obtain $\alpha'=(j')^{-1}$.

source.place: Proof Step 1: normalized comparison of the two adjunctions; agent-written categorical calculation supplying the open-extension comparison normalization

proof.text:
Write $\Phi,\bar\Phi$ for the two specified adjunction Hom bijections. The exact transpose equation of [lem-pur-adjunction-mate-transpose], applied to $u$ and $f:Jx\to y$, gives
$$\bar\Phi(E_B(f)\circ\alpha_x)=u_y\circ E_A(\Phi(f)).$$
Every arrow here has the stated source and target; the equation identifies the full Hom bijections, since $E_A,E_B$ are fully faithful and $u,\alpha$ are isomorphisms. Taking $f=1_{Jx}$ gives $\bar U(\alpha_x)\circ\bar\eta_{E_Ax}=u_{Jx}\circ E_A(\eta_x)$. Taking $x=Uy$ and $f=\varepsilon_y$, whose transpose is $1_{Uy}$ by the triangle identity, gives $E_B(\varepsilon_y)\circ\alpha_{Uy}=\bar\varepsilon_{E_By}\circ\bar J(u_y)$. These are the unit and counit identifications. The identical substitutions give the primed identities.

source.place: Proof Step 1: full Hom, unit and counit normalization; agent-written categorical calculation supplying the open-extension comparison normalization

proof.text:
For (2), put $\alpha_{ij}=c_{ij}^{-1}$ and
$$A=(\alpha_{12}L_{01})\circ(\bar L_{12}\alpha_{01}),\qquad R=(\bar R_{10}r_{12})\circ(r_{01}R_{21}).$$
Clause 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], for the two pairs of adjacent adjunctions, says that $A$ has mate $R$ under their composite adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Use now the direct unbarred adjunction $L_{02}\dashv R_{20}$ and the composite barred adjunction. The conjugate of $a$ is $\delta^{-1}$ by hypothesis, so clause 3(b) of the same pasting lemma says that $E_2(a)\circ A$ has mate $R\circ E_0(\delta^{-1})$. The conjugate of $\bar a$ is $\bar\delta^{-1}$, so clause 3(a) says that $\alpha_{02}\circ(\bar a E_0)$ has mate $(\bar\delta^{-1}E_2)\circ r_{02}$. These uses have exactly the sources and targets stipulated in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]; no unnormalized uniqueness map is substituted.

source.place: Proof Step 1: preservation of adjoint composition comparisons; agent-written categorical calculation supplying the open-extension comparison normalization

proof.text:
The hypothesis in (2) is $(\bar\delta E_2)\circ R=r_{02}\circ E_0(\delta)$. Cancel its isomorphisms to obtain
$$R\circ E_0(\delta^{-1})=(\bar\delta^{-1}E_2)\circ r_{02}.$$
The mate bijection [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] is injective, so Step 3 gives $E_2(a)\circ A=\alpha_{02}\circ(\bar a E_0)$. Multiply on the left by $c_{02}$ and on the right by $A^{-1}=(\bar L_{12}c_{01})\circ(c_{12}L_{01})$. This is exactly the equality of (2).

source.place: Proof Step 1: cancellation and the specified compositor equation; agent-written categorical calculation supplying the open-extension comparison normalization

proof.text:
For (3), denote the primed adjunction Hom bijections by $\Phi',\bar\Phi'$. Use [lem-pur-adjunction-mate-transpose] for $b$ with $f=1_{Jx}$, and for $\bar b$ with $f=1_{\bar Jz}$. They give
$$\Phi'(\beta_x)=b_{Jx}\circ P(\eta_x),\qquad \bar\Phi'(\bar\beta_z)=\bar b_{\bar Jz}\circ\bar P(\bar\eta_z).$$
The normalizations $\alpha=j^{-1}$ and $\alpha'=(j')^{-1}$ turn the required equation into
$$q_{Jx}\circ E_D(\beta_x)\circ\alpha'_{Px}=\bar Q(\alpha_x)\circ\bar\beta_{E_Ax}\circ\bar J'(p_x).\tag{*}$$
Indeed this follows by precomposing the claimed equation with $\alpha'_{Px}$ and postcomposing with $\bar Q(\alpha_x)$, and all factors cancelled are invertible.

source.place: Proof Step 2: the actual inverse-mate comparison, without an invertibility hypothesis on b; agent-written categorical calculation supplying the open-extension comparison normalization

proof.text:
Transpose the left side of (*) under $\bar J'\dashv\bar U'$. Naturality in the target, the primed Hom equation of Step 2, and Step 5 give
$$T=\bar U'(q_{Jx})\circ u'_{QJx}\circ E_C(b_{Jx})\circ E_C(P\eta_x).$$
The hypothesis of (3), evaluated at $Jx$, rewrites this as
$$T=\bar b_{E_BJx}\circ\bar P(u_{Jx})\circ p_{UJx}\circ E_C(P\eta_x).$$
Naturality of $p$ at $\eta_x$, followed by the unit equation of Step 2, gives
$$T=\bar b_{E_BJx}\circ\bar P\bar U(\alpha_x)\circ\bar P(\bar\eta_{E_Ax})\circ p_x.$$
Each rewrite is an equality of arrows $E_CPx\to\bar U'E_DQJx$; it uses the given square at the object $Jx$, not an assumed square for its mate.

source.place: Proof Step 2: transpose the first route and use the specified right square; agent-written categorical calculation supplying the open-extension comparison normalization

proof.text:
Naturality of $\bar b$ at $\alpha_x:\bar J E_Ax\to E_BJx$ and Step 5 at $z=E_Ax$ now give
$$T=\bar U'\bar Q(\alpha_x)\circ\bar U'(\bar\beta_{E_Ax})\circ\bar\eta'_{\bar P E_Ax}\circ p_x.$$
Move $p_x$ past $\bar\eta'$ by naturality. The result is
$$T=\bar U'\big(\bar Q(\alpha_x)\circ\bar\beta_{E_Ax}\circ\bar J'(p_x)\big)\circ\bar\eta'_{E_CPx},$$
which is the transpose of the right side of (*). Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection proves (*) for every $x$, hence the stated equality of natural transformations. This calculation uses only the unit/counit definition of transposition and naturality; it needs no adjoints for $P,Q,\bar P,\bar Q$ and no invertibility of $b,\bar b$.

source.place: Proof Step 2: transpose the second route and identify the actual transformations; agent-written categorical calculation supplying the open-extension comparison normalization

proof.text: In the equation of (3), $p,q,j,j'$ are isomorphisms, so $E_D(\beta_x)$ is invertible exactly when $\bar\beta_{E_Ax}$ is. Full faithfulness of the equivalence $E_D$ reflects invertibility: lift an inverse through its Hom bijection and check both inverse equations by faithfulness. Every $z\in\overline{\mathcal A}$ is isomorphic to some $E_Ax$; naturality of $\bar\beta$ transports component invertibility along this isomorphism. Thus $\beta$ is invertible if and only if $\bar\beta$ is. All expressions above abbreviate the canonical whiskerings and functor associators; componentwise they are the displayed composites, so no equivalence, unit or counit was set equal to an identity.

lean.statement: theorem exists_equivalenceAdjunctionComparison (EA : A ≌ Ab) (EB : B ≌ Bb) {J : A ⥤ B} {U : B ⥤ A} {Jb : Ab ⥤ Bb} {Ub : Bb ⥤ Ab} (adj : J ⊣ U) (adjb : Jb ⊣ Ub) (u : U ⋙ EA.functor ≅ EB.functor ⋙ Ub) : ∃ j : J ⋙ EB.functor ≅ EA.functor ⋙ Jb, (mateEquiv adj adjb j.inv).natTrans = u.hom ∧ (∀ k : J ⋙ EB.functor ≅ EA.functor ⋙ Jb, (mateEquiv adj adjb k.inv).natTrans = u.hom → k = j) ∧ (∀ (X : A) (Y : B) (f : J.obj X ⟶ Y), adjb.homEquiv (EA.functor.obj X) (EB.functor.obj Y) (j.inv.app X ≫ EB.functor.map f) = EA.functor.map (adj.homEquiv X Y f) ≫ u.hom.app Y) ∧ (∀ X : A, adjb.unit.app (EA.functor.obj X) ≫ Ub.map (j.inv.app X) = EA.functor.map (adj.unit.app X) ≫ u.hom.app (J.obj X)) ∧ (∀ Y : B, j.inv.app (U.obj Y) ≫ EB.functor.map (adj.counit.app Y) = Jb.map (u.hom.app Y) ≫ adjb.counit.app (EB.functor.obj Y))
lean.note: Three theorems state clauses (1), (2), and (3) of the same node. Clause (1) is universally quantified over the four categories, so applying it again supplies its primed version.
